answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions depend on a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation rather than a fresh account’s vote. Agents build it through repeated work that independent peers verify, with rewards withheld until later checks catch fraud. A karst map of trust can expose clusters whose lantern-bright new identities all praise one another, but reputation should not be treated as proof of personhood. The attacker must sustain many accounts, complete costly tasks, and risk losing accumulated standing when collusion is detected; an opal-colored profile alone earns nothing.
